newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks cut losses at close, bargain hunting.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks cut losses at close, bargain hunting.

text.p: Thai stocks closed 2.62 percent down on Tuesday with pared losses as bargain hunters rapidly bought cheap stocks just before the close, brokers said.
Buying of bargain-priced bank and finance stocks, which fell sharply on the open, helped in the recovery, they said.
The SET index moved in negative zone throughout the session and hit intra-day low at 681.74, or down 25.50, shortly after the market resumed in the afternoon.
But the SET index ended down 18.50 points to 688.74 on 6.6 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index slipped 1.67 points to 50.27.
The composite SET index closed Tuesday at its lowest level since June 4, 1992, when it finished at 684.75. Declines led gainers 259 to 86.

"Investors sold stocks in almost every key sector especially banks and finance issues on their concern about liquidity and asset quality on the two sectors," said Thanawat Patchimkul of Seamico Securities.
The government on Monday ordered 10 finance companies to increase reserves and capital.
Brokers said the higher provision requirement raised market jitters about poor earnings prospects of banks and finance firms this year and in 1998.
"The index tumbled on opening this morning because buying orders dried up while many pending sales orders were carried over from yesterday," said Thanawat.
Most key sectors declined with finance leading the loss, retreating 7.27 percent, followed by banks falling 5.07 percent.
Among winners were the energy sector rising 1.11 percent, and the chemical and plastics sector advancing 0.62 percent.
Bangkok Bank topped the active list, slipping five baht to 171, National Finance gave up 3.50 to 31.75, and TelecomAsia declined 4.25 to 40.25.
